stage_b_config_issues: rushstack-pnpm-version-supported (07) has no if_present. Removing pnpmVersion from rush.json fires it, which is a false positive for an npm or yarn repo, where Rush does not run this check. The regex also passes a prerelease such as 5.0.0-beta.1, which Rush rejects (semver.lt against MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_PNPM_VERSION '5.0.0' in SetupChecks.ts). R4 holds on the clone, but the rule is looser and stricter than the unit in different places.

rushstack-local-deps-use-workspace-protocol (03) over-asserts. WorkspaceInstallManager.ts:195-316 applies the workspace: check only to Version and Range specifiers, and skips npm: aliases, tags, file: and catalog: specifiers (and peer dependencies). The rule fires on those specifier forms too. It passes at the pin, so this is a latent false positive.

rushstack-command-line-no-global-plugin-commands is labelled under 09b (schema validation after defaults). It expresses a different loader check, the globalPlugin rejection in _prepareRepoCommandLineJson (CommandLineConfiguration.ts:750-770).

The rushstack-09 schema rule set is incomplete. Rush also schema-validates per-project config/rush-project.json (and the rigs/*/profiles/*/config copies), the cached plugin command-line.json (raw, through tryLoadFromFile), and CHANGELOG.json during rush version --bump (ChangelogGenerator.ts:184). I checked that all three pass at the pin with json_schema_passes.

rushstack-57 (subspace config folder exists) covers only subspaceNames. Subspace.ts:154 also requires the folder of the implicit default subspace. A dir_exists on common/config/subspaces/default would cover that (the name is Rush's constant).

rushstack-23 uses dir_only_contains, which is case-sensitive. Rush's _validateCommonRushConfigFolder (RushConfiguration.ts:1555-1632) builds its known set case-insensitively, so a differently-cased known file name gives a false positive.
rushstack-01 evidence: the per-subspace ensureConsistentVersions call that install runs is in cli/actions/BaseInstallAction.ts:175-187, not doBasicInstallAsync.ts:39.

changes.detail: Added if_present: true, so a repo without pnpmVersion (npm or yarn) passes, as in Rush. The regex now encodes semver order against 5.0.0: 6+ majors, 5.x.y above 5.0.0 including prereleases, and 5.0.0 with optional +build. Fires on 4.14.4 and on 5.0.0-beta.1. Passes on 5.0.0, 5.0.1-beta.1, 6.0.0-rc.0 and the clone (10.27.0). With pnpmVersion replaced by npmVersion or removed it does not fire; rushstack-52 still fires on the removal.

matches now accepts every non-Version/Range specifier: workspace:, anything containing ':' or '/', and tag-shaped values. Peers were already excluded. Fires on ^5.0.0, 5.0.0, x, *, '', v5.0.0 and ~5.0.0 for rush-lib's node-core-library dep. Passes on latest, next, xyz, npm:..., file:..., catalog:, link:..., ../path, github:..., 'workspace: *' and the clone. Documented approximation: a tag or tarball starting with a digit is treated as a range.

Changed the source filter from !search(...,'^workspace:') to search(..., <positive Version/Range regex>), so aliases, tags and file/catalog/git specs no longer count as non-workspace. This carries the same over-assertion fix to part 2. For -heft: fires when rush-lib's dep goes workspace:* -> 1.3.4, ^1.3.4 or ''; passes on latest, npm:@rushstack/heft@1.3.4 and file:...; passes on the clone.

Rush matches known names case-insensitively, so each known name is now a per-letter character-class glob. Harmless extensions and deploy-*.json stay case-sensitive, as in Rush. Explicit .npmrc entries were dropped because '.*' covers them. Experiments.JSON now passes (Stage A's rule fired on it), as do PNPM-LOCK.YAML, deploy-x.json, notes.md and .DS_Store. foo.json and Readme.MD fire. Passes on the clone.

New registry_paths_resolve rule. A regex over subspaces.json captures an empty entry only when "subspacesEnabled": true, and that entry resolves against base common/config/subspaces/default. This covers the implicit default subspace that rule 57 missed. Fires when that folder is removed; passes once subspacesEnabled is set false; passes on the clone. Limitation, noted in a comment: a raw-text match, so a minified one-line file would not trigger it.

Completes the 09 schema set:
- rushstack-schema-rush-project: */*/config/rush-project.json (56) and rigs/*/profiles/*/config/rush-project.json (8) vs rush-project.schema.json. Raw per-file validation approximates Rush's validation of the merged extends chain; this is noted in a comment.
- rushstack-schema-plugin-command-line: the cached plugin command-line.json vs command-line.schema.json.
- rushstack-schema-changelog: */*/CHANGELOG.json (83) vs changelog.schema.json.
All pass on the clone. Each fires on a mutation: an unknown key in a project file and in a rig-profile file, commandKind 'nonsense', and a renamed 'entries'.

json_path_absent for the min >= 1 and max >= min sanity checks, using Rush's defaults (min 1, max 2) when a field is absent. Fires with projectFolderMinDepth 3 (max 2) and with 0. Passes with min removed, with max 5, and on the clone.

json_path_matches $.phases[*].name '^_phase:[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$' over the repo command-line.json and the cached plugin command-line.json (if_present). Fires on _phase:Test; passes on the clone.

Four cross_file subset rules (self/upstream deps, phased-command phases, watchPhases, associatedPhases) against $.phases[*].name. For associatedPhases the target also includes bulk-command names, which become synthetic phases. Each fires on its own mutation (self dep -> _phase:nope, pack phases -> _phase:packx, watchPhases -> _phase:nope, associatedPhases -> _phase:packx), and the phase rename fires the three that reference _phase:test. A bulk command named in associatedPhases passes. All pass on the clone.

json_path_absent for a missing or empty associatedCommands, over the repo and plugin files. Plus a cross_file subset of associatedCommands (build and rebuild excluded as restated synthesized commands, the C tuning) against $.commands[*].name. Fires with [] or a renamed key, with 'startx', and when the plugin parameter's associatedCommands is removed. 'rebuild' passes. Passes on the clone.

json_path_absent $.phases[?(@.ignoreMissingScript && @.missingScriptBehavior)] (existence semantics, like Rush's !== undefined). Fires when ignoreMissingScript: false is added next to missingScriptBehavior; passes on the clone.

json_path_absent for a build/rebuild that is global, globalPlugin or safeForSimultaneousRushProcesses == true. Fires with build's commandKind set to global and with safeForSimultaneousRushProcesses: true; passes on the clone.

json_path_absent with match() against the 26 built-in action names, read from rush-lib's actions and restated (C), over the repo and plugin command-line files. Fires when prettier is renamed to install and when the plugin command is renamed to publish; passes on installx and the clone.

unit_notes.note: Its only rule, rushstack-command-line-no-global-plugin-commands, expresses a different loader check: the globalPlugin rejection at CommandLineConfiguration.ts ~749-770. That check should be recorded as its own A unit (other); the rule passes on the clone and fires on mutation. 09b (schema validation after build defaults) keeps C but now has no rule, because the shim schema it needs cannot live outside the repo and still replay standalone.

Stage B proposed C because its for_each_dir form over-asserted on unreferenced autoinstallers. The integrated rule takes its target from command-line.json, keeping only global commands whose autoinstallerName equals the folder's basename, with allow_missing_target. Unreferenced autoinstallers therefore pass (verified: renaming the plugins autoinstaller's package name does not fire). Together with the name-regex and registry_paths_resolve rules, this expresses GlobalScriptAction.ts ~63-102 exactly.

No in-repo, standalone form exists. json_schema_passes has no inline schema, a shim schema outside the clone cannot replay, and JSONPath cannot read member names, so the C form Stage B proposed cannot be built under the standalone-replay rule. It needs key access (the entry adapter) with a regex predicate. The integrator decides between B-config and keeping C with no rule.

Schema, rigPackageName and rigProfile checks are expressed and fire-verified. The profile-folder-exists sub-check is not expressed, because RigConfig resolves the rig package through node_modules (package resolution) and registry_paths_resolve cannot template a base per file. If the integrator counts that sub-check as part of the unit, it stays unexpressed.

The implicit default subspace folder is now covered by rushstack-default-subspace-config-folder-exists. Its condition reads subspacesEnabled from the raw text of subspaces.json through a regex, so the bucket stays A with that caveat.
